newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end at record high on NY opening.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end at record high on NY opening.

text.p: Swedish shares ended at record high levels on Thursday, after coming off day lows when New York opened higher.
The general index rose 0.27 percent to 2,435.50 in turnover of 5.50 billion crowns.
Metals and mining group Trelleborg and telecommunications group Ericsson were in focus.

Trelleborg surged 11 crowns to 108 on rumours that it planned to spin-off its Boliden subsidiary. The company declined to comment on the rumours but said it is in an important development phase which will give the company a new structure.
Ericsson kept advancing ahead of U.S. rival Motorola's earnings report, due later on Thursday. The share rose four crowns to 226 crowns, building on its 14 crown gain a day earlier.
The bank and insurance sector was the loser, down 1.46 percent after a newspaper article said the government is likely to sell its 59 percent Nordbanken stake to investors.
This dampened hopes for a merger between S-E-Banken and Nordbanken. Nordbanken dropped five crowns to 220 crowns, while S-E-Banken shed one and landed at 70 crowns.
